e: Parts of a plaster ceiling collapse at a supermarket in Daegu, injuring 38 people.
South Korea recalls its ambassador to Ukraine, citing the latter's decision to reveal the transfer of North Korean POWs the previous month.

K-pop singer and Winner member Mino is convicted of failing 102 times to report at a community center in Seoul as part of an alternative arrangement under the military service act and is sentenced to a suspended one-year prison term.
Ukraine announces that two North Korean soldiers that had been captured while fighting for Russia had been transferred to South Korea.
Three soldiers are injured in a suspected landmine explosion along the DMZ.
The Yeosu World Island Exhibition is held in Yeosu, South Jeolla Province.
One person is killed in a crane collapse caused by strong winds generated by Tropical Storm Krovanh in the Port of Jeju.
A court sentences an elderly care home director in Incheon to 15 years' imprisonment for sexually assaulting three of his patients.
A court in Seoul sentences Unification Church leader Han Hak-ja to two years' imprisonment for bribery involving former first lady Kim Keon Hee.
A police officer is arrested for issuing false information following the discovery of four bodies linked to missing persons cases in Jeju Province.

US President Donald Trump orders the Pentagon to reduce annual joint military exercises with South Korea, saying that the latter refused to help with the 2026 Iran war and citing his good relationship with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.
One person is killed in a landslide in Geoje.
Two former Chinese military officers are arrested in separate incidents on suspicion of spying.

The Korea Aerospace Research Institute announces the successful test flight of the first domestically developed high-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle capable of operating at altitudes exceeding 12 kilometers for more than 24 hours.
The getbol tidal flats are designated as UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

A special investigation team consisting of police and prosecutors raids the headquarters and branches of the National Election Commission over allegations that some employees manipulated data to cover up errors in the voter turnout count from the June 3 local elections.
The first vehicle rolls off the production line at the newly built KGM Commercial electric truck plant in Gunsan.

The National Assembly passes a bill to abolish the Ministry of Unification, transferring its functions to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other relevant departments, in line with the current administration's realignment of inter-Korean policy.

The Supreme Court upholds the 7-year prison sentence and 5-year suspended sentence for former President Yoon Suk Yeol, who was convicted on charges of inciting insurrection and interfering with official duties by ordering his security service to block the execution of a court warrant.
The Ministry of Science and ICT officially launches the state-run artificial intelligence company "K-AGI" to boost national competitiveness in the AI sector.
Kim Min-seok resigns as prime minister and is replaced by Han Seong-sook.
Lee Man-hee, the founder of the Shincheonji Church of Jesus, is arrested on charges of electoral interference over the recruitment of thousands of followers into the People Power Party.
Former justice minister Park Sung-jae is sentenced to 25 years' imprisonment for his role in abetting the imposition of martial law in 2024.
Former president Yoon Suk Yeol is sentenced to 30 years' imprisonment for sending drones into North Korea as part of efforts to stage provocations to justify the imposition of martial law in 2024.
The PIPC issues a 624.6 billion won ($400 million) fine on Coupang over a 2025 data breach that exposed around 37.5 million users.
Public assemblies and citizen gatherings continue following the shortage of ballots in local elections, primarily centered around the Olympic Handball Gymnasium in Jamsil-dong, Seoul.
An explosion hits a factory operated by Hanwha Aerospace in Daejeon, killing five people.
An overpass demolition site in Seodaemun District, Seoul, collapses, killing three people and injuring three others.
Naegohyang Women's FC wins the 2025–26 AFC Women's Champions League after defeating Tokyo Verdy Beleza 1–0 at the final in Suwon.
North Korean team Naegohyang Women's FC defeats South Korean side Suwon FC Women at the semifinals of the AFC Women's Champions League in Suwon.
North Korean team Naegohyang Women's FC arrive in Incheon to compete at the AFC Women's Champions League in Suwon, the first time a North Korean sports team has been sent to the South since 2018.
The Seoul High Court sentences former president Yoon Suk Yeol to seven years' imprisonment on charges related to the 2024 South Korean martial law crisis.
The Seoul High Court extends former first lady Kim Keon Hee's prison term for corruption from 20 months to four years.
Fourteen people are killed in a fire at a car parts factory in Daejeon.
A child is injured after being hit at a playground by a stray bullet suspected to have been fired during nearby military exercises in Daegu.
Police raid the headquarters of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport in Sejong City as part of a renewed investigation into the crash of Jeju Air Flight 2216 in 2024.
President Lee orders the activation of a ₩100 trillion (about US$68 billion) stabilization fund to address volatility in the country's financial markets linked to the 2026 Iran war.
A Truth and Reconciliation Commission is convened to investigate anomalies in the international adoption of South Korean children.
An F-16 fighter jet of the Republic of Korea Air Force crashes near Yeongju, North Gyeongsang Province. The pilot safely ejects.
Former president Yoon Suk Yeol is convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment for insurrection relating to the 2024 South Korean martial law crisis.
